conversation.content:
Good morning, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—I spend my days helping new mothers sort through the huge emotional swings that can come after a baby arrives. Today we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, usually called the EPDS. It’s a brief 10-question screen that helps us see how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past week, so we can be sure you’re getting exactly the support you need. Everything you share stays confidential between you and the clinical team, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever is true for you. We’ll move through one question at a time; each one simply asks you to pick the response that best matches how often you’ve felt a certain way. Ready to begin?

Here’s the first one:

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, I’ve got a newborn who wakes up every couple of hours and a toddler who’s jealous of the baby—so genuine laughter feels pretty rare right now. Maybe once or twice I’ve cracked a small smile at something on my phone, but it’s nowhere near the easy laughter I used to have.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most of the time, no—I haven’t really laughed. Maybe once or twice something tiny made me smile, but it’s like the lightness just isn’t there anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much lately. I used to get excited about little plans—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but now it feels like I’m just dragging myself through the day. I’ll think “that could be nice,” but the spark never really catches.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… pretty often. If the baby won’t settle or I can’t get the toddler dressed without a meltdown, my head jumps straight to “I’m failing at this.” Even when I know rationally it’s not all on me, I still catch myself thinking I should be doing better.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Definitely. A lot of the time I’m on edge, even when everything looks fine on the outside. I’ll lie down after a feeding and suddenly my heart’s racing, imagining the baby’s breathing changed or that I missed a burp and she’ll choke. Nothing specific happened—my mind just spins.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes, that’s been happening. Sometimes out of nowhere I get this wave of panic—like my chest tightens and I feel I can’t catch my breath. There’s no real danger, just this awful sense that something bad is about to happen, and I have to pace the hallway or grip the crib rail until it passes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days it feels like I’m drowning a little. Between the night feedings, the toddler clinging to my leg, and the housework piling up, I keep thinking, “I can’t keep up.” I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling through everything I think I did wrong that day—why the baby cried so long, how I snapped at my toddler, whether I’m already ruining them. I’ll finally drift off, but then I jolt awake sure I heard the baby, and the whole cycle starts again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll look at the baby and feel love, but it’s quickly followed by this wave of sadness I can’t shake, even when nothing bad is happening right then.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, I’ve cried—maybe three or four times in the past week. It’s usually when I’m alone, like when the baby finally naps and the house is quiet, and I just feel this rush of sadness and guilt. Sometimes I don’t even know exactly why I’m crying—it just spills out.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel overwhelmed and low, but hurting myself hasn’t crossed my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

Patient-reported symptoms:
- Marked anhedonia (minimal laughter, loss of anticipatory enjoyment)
- Daily low mood, frequent crying spells, pervasive “heaviness”
- Excessive self-blame and guilt concerning parenting performance
- Persistent, unprovoked anxiety and panic symptoms (racing heart, chest tightness, fear of imminent harm)
- Sleep disruption driven by intrusive rumination and hypervigilance regarding infant safety
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed and “drowning” in daily demands

Patterns consistent with:
- Major depressive symptoms with postpartum onset
- Comorbid anxiety/panic features

Safety:
- Denies self-harm or suicidal ideation (endorsed item 10 negatively)

Screening significance:
Elevated risk for moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety; further clinical evaluation recommended to clarify diagnosis and determine level of care.
